name: L1 nine answers, the second thing, point number five
text: Okay so I am going to answer the questions one by one. The first thing is the pricing, and honestly I think we should keep it simple, one plan for everybody, because every time we add tiers people ask which tier they need and then nobody buys anything. Yeah so one plan, matlab flat price, and maybe a discount if they pay for the year. I know some people will say we are leaving money on the table, but I would rather have a price that fits in one sentence. The second thing is the free trial. I would say fourteen days is enough, and we do not ask for a card, because asking for a card at the start kills the signups, and I have seen that happen on the last two products. Okay. The third thing is onboarding. So when somebody installs it the first screen should just ask for the microphone permission and nothing else, and then it should say press the key and speak, haan, that is all, no tour, no settings, because the settings can come later once they like it. The fourth point is the languages. We need Hindi and English mixed together to work properly, theek hai, because that is how most of us actually talk, and if the app breaks on a Hindi word in the middle of an English sentence people will stop trusting it. Point number five is the pill on the screen. I want it small by default, and it should never steal focus. I tried a big one once and it felt like the app was shouting at me, so small is better. When it is recording it should show clearly that it is listening, but not in a loud way, accha, so just a small dot and the level. Sixth is retention. So what brings people back is that it saves them time every single day, so we should show a small counter of how many words they spoke this week, and maybe not too much more than that. Yeah. Streaks and badges feel childish to me and I would not add them. Seventh, the privacy. Everything should stay on the machine by default, and if we use any cloud model for the formatting we should say so clearly in the settings, with a switch to turn it off. The AI disclaimer should be on by default so nobody is surprised. People should be able to read in one screen exactly what leaves the machine. I would also keep the history off until somebody turns it on, because a lot of what people say is private. The eighth question is about the engine budget. I think we should cap the cloud calls to one per dictation, because the cost adds up quickly, and if it times out we just use the local result and move on. If the model is down for a day nobody should even notice, that is the whole point of the fallback. And number nine is the launch. Let us do a small launch with maybe fifty people we know, collect what breaks, fix it for two weeks, and only then put it on the public pages. Once that is stable we can announce it properly, with a short video and a page that explains what it does in one sentence, and then see who actually comes back after a week, because that number tells us more than any survey would. That is it, yeah, that is all my answers. Please write them down in the doc.
